Logistic Regression: Mortgage Denial Pima County HMDA 2025

Analytical Sample

For the logistic regression, we restrict the sample to applications that were either originated or denied. Originated applications are coded as 0 (not denied), while denied applications are coded as 1. Other outcomes (approved but not accepted, withdrawn, incomplete, purchased, and other application outcomes) are excluded because they do not represent a directly comparable approval-versus-denial decision.

Keeping only originated and denied applications i.e. action_taken values: 1 = originated and 3 = denied

pima_hmda_clean keeps only rows that have an interest rate, and denied applicants never get one, so all denials (action_taken == 3) are deleted during cleaning. A logistic regression on denial needs both outcomes (denied = 1, approved = 0).

```{r}
source("data_cleaned.R")

table(pima_logistic$denial)

num_samples <- nrow(pima_logistic)

# 70-30 split
set.seed(42)
train_index <- as.numeric(sample(rownames(pima_logistic), 0.7 * num_samples))
train_data <- pima_logistic[train_index, ]
test_data  <- pima_logistic[-train_index, ]

logistic_model <- glm(
  denial ~ income + loan_amount + property_value,
  data = train_data,
  family = binomial
)

summary(logistic_model)

# Multicollinearity check
vif(logistic_model)

B_0 <- -0.593      # intercept
B_1 <- 9.19e-06    # income (per $1,000)
B_2 <- -3.72e-06   # loan_amount (per $1)
B_3 <- -2.09e-09   # property_value (per $1)

# Predicted probabilities on the test set
test_data$predicted_prob <- predict(logistic_model, newdata = test_data, type = "response")

# 0.5 threshold: at or above 0.5 is predicted as denied (1)
test_data$predicted_class <- ifelse(test_data$predicted_prob >= 0.5, 1, 0)

# Confusion matrix and test accuracy
table(Predicted = test_data$predicted_class, Actual = test_data$denial)
mean(test_data$predicted_class == test_data$denial)


#Illustratively picked values

income <- 100               # which is basically $100,000
property_value <- 350000

# Applicant A: loan amount $150,000
loan_amount <- 150000
log_odds_A = B_0 + B_1*income + B_2*loan_amount + B_3*property_value
odds_A = exp(log_odds_A)                       #(p/1-p)
probability_A <- exp(log_odds_A) / (1 + exp(log_odds_A))

# Applicant B: same income and property value, loan amount $350,000
loan_amount <- 350000
log_odds_B = B_0 + B_1*income + B_2*loan_amount + B_3*property_value
odds_B = exp(log_odds_B)
probability_B <- exp(log_odds_B) / (1 + exp(log_odds_B))

probability_A / probability_B      #Applicant A's chance of denial is 1.8 times than B's

pred_data <- data.frame(loan_amount = seq(50000, 1000000, by = 25000))
pred_data <- pred_data %>%
  mutate(
    log_odds    = B_0 + B_1*100 + B_2*loan_amount + B_3*350000,
    probability = exp(log_odds) / (1 + exp(log_odds))
  )

ggplot(pred_data, aes(x = loan_amount, y = probability)) +
  geom_line(linewidth = 1.4, color = "steelblue") +
  geom_point(data = data.frame(loan_amount = c(150000, 350000),
                               probability = c(probability_A, probability_B)),
             size = 3, color = "darkred") +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 14) +
  labs(title = "Predicted Probability of Denial by Loan Amount",
       subtitle = "Holding income = $100,000 and property value = $350,000",
       x = "Loan Amount ($)", y = "Predicted Probability of Denial") +
  ylim(0, 1)

```
